paragraph_content.content: The key takeaways from YUMC's solid 2Q26 results earnings call reaffirmed our positive view. Despite a fluid consumption backdrop, YUMC delivered SSSG improvement in 2Q26 and the initial tone for 3Q also shows confidence, ahead of investors' cautious view prior to the results given weak consumption sentiment, unfavorable weather conditions, and a high base last year. Aside from its solid execution track record, new formats/modules (i.e. K coffee Cafe, K Pro, Pizza Hut Burger Bar etc) have delivered solid performance and contributed to the parent stores, opening up new revenue streams; YUMC has further accelerated the new format roll-out. Mgmt comments on the rising chain ratio in the catering industry and disciplined promotion/pricing in the market are also encouraging. Looking ahead, we see solid catalysts from an easier base for margin in 2H on the back of less expense pressure from delivery mix increase. Separately, mgmt noted upside potential from stronger Pizza Hut growth and improved profitability following the acquisition (on track in August 2026, per mgmt). Remain Buy (on CL) with new TP at US$59/HK$459 (prior: US$58/HK$452).

Key highlights from the earnings call include: 1) Looking into 3Q26, management targets positive SSSG and noted that Jul performance has been broadly in line with their expectation; restaurant margin is expected to be stable or slightly up yoy with less headwind from delivery mix yoy increase and continuous cost optimization/efficiency gain, while OPM is expected to be stable or slightly improved yoy though there will be less benefit yoy from government subsidy (per mgmt, they are not including the PH acquisition impact, which they expect will bring 20-30bps OPM benefit in 3Q, in their guidance). Management reiterated confidence in meeting full year guidance without considering the impact from the PH brand acquisition (expected to close in Aug per mgmt), which they expect would have a slightly accretive margin impact this year.

paragraph_content.content: 2) New initiatives' progress encouraging. KCoffee Cafe is on track to reach 5k locations by year end, with sales expected to double yoy to Rmb2bn this year; management revised up KPro opening guidance again to 800 by year end (from 600 prior), and has been expanding this model towards lower tier cities. Meanwhile, several other new initiatives are viewed as promising, including PH Burger side-by-side which has expanded to >200 locations with DD% sales uplift/meaningful profit to parent store, and KFC drive thru which is expected to exceed Rmb1bn sales this year. 3) PH brand acquisition to further unlock growth and margin opportunity per mgmt. Post closing of the acquisition, mgmt expect the company to see 2.8pp benefit to PH restaurant margin (post VAT), which they expect will improve UE and help to lower sales threshold for opening stores that can achieve 2-3 year payback; meanwhile, management highlighted that this will bring more operational flexibility. Management revised up store addition guidance to >800 p.a. in 2027-28, from >600 p.a. prior. Regarding financing, the company will leverage US$1.2bn bridge loan for 12 months first with interest rate of ~2%, and has been evaluating different options for future financing. Management reiterated shareholder return guidance, and they noted the faster growth of PH could also bring benefit to FCF. 4) Comments on competition landscape: management noted pricing trend has been stable, and commented that more rational competition from delivery platforms/ongoing chainification and crackdown on ghost kitchens are tailwinds for the company.
We revised up 2026-28E earnings forecast by

, factoring in 2Q26 results, updated FX assumptions, and yoy margin improvement in 2H. Despite the fluid consumption backdrop, we view YUMC's TAM expansion with strong execution in new initiatives, as well as continuous efficiency gain would support earnings visibility. Our current estimate does not reflect the PH brand acquisition impact.
We would like to thank Mattie, He for her contribution to the report.

title_content.content: Key takeaways from the conference call

paragraph_content.content: Recent trends: Mgmt noted that July trading was broadly in line with expectations despite temporary regional disruptions from extreme weather. Consumer demand remained resilient in coffee, light meals, innovative products and experiences. Pricing trends continued to stabilize, and competition among delivery platforms became more rational. Mgmt noted room for further consolidation by leading brands thanks to the ghost kitchen regulation and outperformance of chain brands vs nationwide retail sales growth.

title_content.content: Outlook on FY26/2H26/3Q26/after PH brand deal/longer-term:

paragraph_content.content: The company reaffirmed its 2026 full-year targets excluding the PH brand deal, including an SSSG of 0-2%, MSD-HSD% system sales growth, HSD% OP growth, DD% EPS growth, and slight improvement in both restaurant margin and OPM. The company also remains on track to reach 20k stores by year-end.

In 3Q26, Mgmt targets positive SSSG and transaction growth. Excluding the PH deal impact, mgmt expects restaurant margin to be stable to slightly positive yoy, as incremental rider-cost pressure moderates. OPM is expected to be broadly flat or slightly improved yoy, partly due to the non-recurrence of government subsidies recorded in 3Q25.

In 2H26, for PH, mgmt expects restaurant margin to show greater yoy improvement than in 1H26, driven by improved efficiency and moderating rider-cost pressure, broadly stable COGS and continued efficiency improvements. Mgmt maintained its FY26 PH COGS guidance of c.34% and the long-term target of ~31% (+/-1%).

Update on the PH brand deal: Mgmt noted the transaction remains on track to close in Aug. Per mgmt, savings from the 3% PH license fee are expected to add c.2.8ppt to PH restaurant margin (after VAT) and c.60bps to Yum China's margin. Mgmt expects the deal should contribute c.30-40bps to restaurant margin and OPM in 3Q26 and c.20-30bps for FY26 after deal costs, financing expenses and tax; they expect EPS impact to be slightly accretive in 2026 and MSD% accretive in 2027-28. Mgmt expects PH net openings to exceed 800 annually in both 2027 and 2028, versus the previous target of over 600.

Financing: The Company is on track to close the acquisition of the Pizza Hut brand in Mainland China in August and plans to secure around $1.2 billion equivalent offshore bridge loan to finance the transaction, which carries ~2% interest rate. Per mgmt, longer-term financing options remain preliminary and may include syndicated loans, bonds, or convertible bonds. If convertible bonds are used, the group is committed to minimizing potential dilution, including capped calls with high premium conversion and net share settlement.

Strategical benefits: Mgmt expects savings in license fees will bring Pizza Hut's restaurant margin closer to KFC's level, enabling more new stores to meet the 2-to-3-year payback requirement. With the improved margin profile, mgmt uplifted the store expansion target. In longer term, mgmt expects the brand's ownership to provide greater operational flexibility, such as product and menu innovation.

KCoffee cafe: Store count reached 3,300 in 2Q26, adding ~700 from the prior quarter. Management aims to double sales yoy to Rmb 2bn in 2026 and continues to target 5k stores by end of 2027. KCoffee Cafe continued to deliver MSD% sales uplift to the parent KFC stores.

Kpro: Store count reached 450+ from 280 in the prior quarter, with ~20% sales uplift to the company store. Management raised targets to 800 store count (up from 600) by year-end. KPRO is delivering ~20% sales uplift to parent KFC stores, showing solid margin improvement, and expanding across Tier 1, Tier 2, and select lower-tier cities. Management expects KPRO sales to quadruple year over year in 2026 and exceed RMB 1bn in 2027.

KFC drive-thru and car-side pickup: The Company has >8,000 KFC drive-thru locations, but active member penetration is only c.3%, leaving significant room for adoption growth. Management targets RMB 1bn in sales from this channel in 2026.

■ PH burger bar: Pizza Hut Burger Bar has been well-received. Within roughly six months, it expanded to 200+ locations and generated DD% incremental sales uplift to parent Pizza Hut stores, with meaningful profit contribution (though initial COS is higher and margin lower than brand's average). Management plans to accelerate it to 500-600 locations by the end of 2026, equivalent to c.10% of the Pizza Hut store base, and targets more than RMB 1bn in sales this year, or c.5-6% of Pizza Hut sales. Management stated that burger sales appear incremental to the group, with the format offering customer choice and differentiated product attributes versus KFC.
■ PH Wow: Pizza Hut Wow stores continue to help the brand penetrate lower-tier cities with store count reaching >400.

Comments on SSSG and store expansion pace: Mgmt noted faster store expansion does not necessarily lead to lower SSSG, citing countermeasures including discovering untapped white space opportunities, strategic channels, prime areas in high tier cities, etc.

Pricing and competition: Mgmt observed continued stabilization in industry pricing, with more players willing to take pricing actions and delivery-platform competition becoming more rational. KFC avg. ticket declined 3% yoy to Rmb36, mainly due to incremental smaller orders from KCoffee, Kpro and other new customer occasions, while transactions grew 4%. PH avg. ticket declined 11% to Rmb68, approaching its Rmb60-70 target range under the mass-market strategy, while transactions increased 13%. Mgmt continues to prioritize traffic, value for money and incremental occasions over headline ticket growth.

Shareholder returns: The company reiterates its plan to return $1.5bn to shareholders in 2026. Starting in 2027, the group reiterates that it will return c. 100% of annual free cash flow after dividends to non-controlling interests, implying $900 million to over $1 billion in 2027 and 2028, and to exceed $1 billion in 2028. In addition, mgmt noted upside potential from stronger Pizza Hut growth and improved profitability following the acquisition.

title_content.content: Price Target Risks and Methodology - Yum China Holdings

paragraph_content.content: Valuation methodology: We are Buy rated on YUMC with 12-m SOTP-based target prices of US\$59/HK\$459 for the ADR/H-share. Our target multiples are 11x 2026E EV/EBITDA for KFC China and 7x for Pizza Hut China.
Key downside risks: 1) weaker-than-expected SSSG; 2) higher-than-expected commodity costs; 3) stronger-than-expected competition; and 4) lower-than-expected execution efficiency.

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.

title_content.content: Ratings, coverage universe and related definitions

paragraph_content.content: Buy (B), Neutral (N), Sell (S) Analysts recommend stocks as Buys or Sells for inclusion on various regional Investment Lists. Being assigned a Buy or Sell on an Investment List is determined by a stock's total return potential relative to its coverage universe. Any stock not assigned as a Buy or a Sell on an Investment List with an active rating (i.e., a stock that is not Rating Suspended, Not Rated, Early-Stage Biotech, Coverage Suspended or Not Covered), is deemed Neutral. Each region manages Regional Conviction Lists, which are selected from Buy rated stocks on the respective region's Investment Lists and represent investment recommendations focused on the size of the total return potential and/or the likelihood of the realization of the return across their respective areas of coverage. The addition or removal of stocks from such Conviction Lists are managed by the Investment Review Committee or other designated committee in each respective region and do not represent a change in the analysts' investment rating for such stocks.

Total return potential represents the upside or downside differential between the current share price and the price target, including all paid or anticipated dividends, expected during the time horizon associated with the price target. Price targets are required for all covered stocks. The total return potential, price target and associated time horizon are stated in each report adding or reiterating an Investment List membership.
Coverage Universe: A list of all stocks in each coverage universe is available by primary analyst, stock and coverage universe at https://www.gs.com/research/hedge.html.

Not Rated (NR). The investment rating, target price and earnings estimates (where relevant) are removed pursuant to GS policy when GS is acting in an advisory capacity in a merger or in a strategic transaction involving this company, when there are legal, regulatory or policy constraints due to GS' involvement in a transaction, and in certain other circumstances. Early-Stage Biotech (ES). An investment rating and a target price are not assigned pursuant to GS policy when this company has neither a drug, treatment or medical device that has passed a Phase II clinical trial nor a license to distribute a post-Phase II drug, treatment or medical device. Rating Suspended (RS). GS has suspended the investment rating and price target for this stock, because there is not a sufficient fundamental basis for determining an investment rating or target price. The previous investment rating and target price, if any, are no longer in effect for this stock and should not be relied upon. Coverage Suspended (CS). GS has suspended coverage of this company. Not Covered (NC). GS does not cover this company.
